recipes.name: Oatmeal Peanut Butter and Chocolate Chip Cookies

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat brown sugar, butter, and white sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until creamy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until combined. Stir in peanut butter, water, and vanilla.

Combine flour and baking soda in a separate bowl. Stir dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined. Stir in oats and chocolate chips. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly toasted on the edges, 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven and transfer to wire racks to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Oatmeal Peanut Butter and Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: If you can’t decide what kind of cookie to make, this peanut butter-oatmeal cookie recipe has it all with a chewy combination of oats, peanut butter, and chocolate chips.

review.reviewBody: I am giving these a strong 5 but with *large adjustments* I made them 3 times to get what I thought was a perfect PB Cookie:I always use part butter part crisco(I like the texture)so.. 1 stick of BUTTER, 1/4 c.Crisco,I use 1 cup of Crunchy PB, 3/4 cups of chocholate chips, 3/4 cups of P.B. chips,I have to use 1/2 cup more flour, I use milk(don't go over the 1/4 c. or they wil get candy like & to soft) I do pop in a pinch of cinnmn. NO nuts..the crunchy pb works great,cook for 14 min. (I live in Oregon) GREAT COOKIE!!

Great starter recipe. I made a lot of changes, as suggested by others. They included: increased peanut butter (smooth) to 1 cup; added ¼ c. whole wheat flour; added ¼c. more oatmeal; added 2 tblsp of hemp powder & flaxseed powder (makes them much more filling!) used ½ & ½ dark chocolate & peanut butter chips (the resulting 1 cup was heaping); used brown sugar substitute; cut the white sugar to ¼ cup. I made larger cookies & baked an additional 2 minutes. Let them cool slightly before removing from pan so they didn't crumble. Even with larger cookies, I still ended up with 33 cookies in this batch. Definitely my new favorite cookie!!! (I'm making my 2nd batch today!)

Excellent recipe but because I'm a diabetic I used Splenda dark sugar blend and Monk fruit to replace the white sugar. I used only 1/4 C monk fruit. I thought they were very flavorable. I removed them from the pan right after taking them out of the oven too.

I would have given this 5 stars but I made many adjustments from other reviewers and they were delicious. I used 1 cup crunchy peanut butter, 1 stick butter, 1/4 cup crisco, 2 cups flour and 1/2 tsp salt and, of course, milk instead of water and baked for 15 mins as we like our cookies more on the crispy side. Those were the only adjustments and next time I am going to try rice krispees as someone mentioned adding them in a review and it sounds really good!

I made some changes: more peanut butter, doubled the baking soda, milk instead of water, more vanilla. Also, refrigerated the dough for an hour or 2, helped them hold together better and not spread out too thin while baking. Baking soda helped with a little more rise and salty flavor. Very good, but still not exactly what I was looking for.

Very delicious. I used 1/2 cup of peanut butter instead of 1/3 cup, and added peanuts (I put them in a bag and slammed them with a metal ladle to crush them a bit) and mixed them in. I scooped closer to a TBSP size dollop for each one, and baked them at 375 degrees for about 11 minutes. The result is a chewy, crunchy, chocolately, peanut-buttery, delicious cookie!

Everyone loved these when i made them! super peanutbuttery i did add 3/4 cup peanut butter and extra 1/4 cup flour and a whole bag of chocolate chips, about 2 cups instead of one. Had to bake an extra minute or two though as i made them rather large scoops lol. Very very yummy!

Increased crunchy p. butter to 3/4 c, added 1/4 c more flour and used whole wheat flour, added 1/4 c more rolled oats and used 1/4 c sugar free vanilla creamer in lieu of water. Used dark chocolate and omitted white sugar. A very healthy delicious cookie!

I've made these cookies in the past with great results. However, My nine year old nephew needs a gluten free diet and often misses out on treats. I made these delightful cookies with a gluten free all purpose flor that I purchased at a health food store. The result was amazing! Hint: instead of dropping onto the tray by spoonfuls, roll into a ball and flatten with a fork.

This was my third time making these and this is definitely one of the best cookies I've ever had. Here's what to change/add:

Use 1 cup pb instead of 1/3
Add1 t cinnamon
Add ½ t salt
Use ¼ cup more of flour

And bake for 14 minutes. It's best to make the cookies a little smaller to make sure the middle gets done. They fall apart right out of the oven but after a couple of minutes they will stay together easily. So good.

I read the review BEFORE I made these. There were some good suggestions and I too made the following adjustments: I used 1/4 cup of milk instead of water. I used 1 3/4 c of flour and 1/4 tsp more baking powder (not soda - either is fine)and 1 c of crunchy peanut butter. I also used 1/2 a bag of semi sweet choc chips. I used the other ingredients as directed in the original recipe. I baked for 12 minutes (set kitchen timer). The cookies came out perfect. approx 30-40 cookies depending how large the drops are - I used a tablespoon not a teaspoon
So delightful, I switched out some chocolate chips for butterscotch, dark chocolate and semi sweet. I added a 1/4 cup of each chip! Awesome recipe.
I’ve made this a half dozens times and I love it! It has it all! I pretty much follow the recipe as written but sometimes I add nuts, sometimes I put in cinnamon. It’s always good. Enjoy
Great recipe! Added extra peanut butter.. made it half cup PB plus. Will make again👍🏻

I have made this recipe once exactly as written. It was perfect! I was actually looking for a cookie that I could add to. Again, perfect! I now make this recipe exactly as written with the addition of walnuts and micro greens. It’s a delicious quick breakfast snack. I’d like to add raisins, next. But, for now, I’ll enjoy this last batch without~

These cookies are delicious! My grandson said I’m the best cookie baker in the whole world! I doubled the batch so I had plenty to share. The only thing I did different was I chilled the dough for about an hour (I needed a little break) that is it. I will make these often, by request from my family. Thank you so much for the recipe!

I just made these for a church function my mom has tomorrow and this recipe produced 37 large cookies and took 14 minutes to bake. The size is what I would term "Grandma cookies". But they are wonderful and most. I have never been disappointed in any of the recipes I have found on this website. This one is a definite keeper for us. I will probably be adding this to the 4 cookies I already make for Christmas.
This and the old, original oatmeal cookie from the Quaker Oats box, I used chocolate chips rather than raisins, are my favorite cookie recipes.
